text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (31.5%, 6.3%, 5.61, 4.99, 24 documented, 4 of 4 supported, 3 of 16). The inconclusive framing and next steps are sensible and cautious. But the headline claim \"far above expectation in every complexity tier\" is not supported: the card gives only the provider's own 99215 share by tier and an all-provider share, with no expected share by tier, and the 0-condition tier has 1 of 18 (5.6%) against 1.8% on tiny counts. The narrative also contradicts itself, saying \"not explained by panel mix alone\" while also saying most 99215s are on multi-morbid patients. The reasoning that high MDM is \"surprising\" on 1-condition patients, and the inference of templating from it, is speculative and weakly grounded. The listed next steps are generic and omit the specific claim IDs that the rationale names.","problems":["Headline overstates: \"every complexity tier\" is not tied to an expected benchmark, and tier counts are small (e.g., 1 of 18 at 0 conditions).","Rationale is internally inconsistent (\"not explained by panel mix alone\" vs \"most 99215s on multi-morbid patients\"; the 4.98x ratio is not mentioned).","Speculation about templating or cloned notes rests on 3 claims and 2 low-condition-count examples, with no evidence of cloning.","Structured next_steps are generic, are not tied to specific claim IDs, and leave out the prioritization described in the rationale; \"Re-screen\" is vague.","Cited example claims C0114066 and C0114074 are low-complexity but have no documentation, so they support little beyond the age and condition-count facts.","The 3 data-reviewed notes without a lab line are not identified by claim ID."]}
